messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed in our universe is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a mass of roughly **20 Jupiter masses** (about 0.02 solar masses). Because it sits right at the boundary between massive planets and low‑mass brown dwarfs, some researchers consider it a “super‑planet” or a “proto‑brown dwarf,” but it is still classified as a planet rather than a star.

Key facts:

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Mass** | ~20 M<sub>J</sub> (≈0.02 M<sub>☉</sub>) |
| **Radius** | ~2–3 R<sub>J</sub> (estimates vary) |
| **Orbital distance** | ~10–15 AU from its host star |
| **Age of system** | ~5–10 Myr (very young) |

Because HD 100546 b is still accreting material and is embedded in a protoplanetary disk, its exact size and mass are still being refined. Nonetheless, it remains the most massive planet known to date.
